title: Global Variable Injection via extract() and parse_str()
platform_conditions: PHP 7.4/8.x; register_globals is gone since PHP 5.4 — extract() and one-argument parse_str() (deprecated since 7.2, still functional) are the remaining symbol-table import paths
security_mechanism: extract() imports every array key as a variable in the current scope, and parse_str() called without a destination array registers query-string keys as local variables, so a POST body containing is_admin=1 creates $is_admin that later authorization code reads instead of application state. $_REQUEST merges GET, POST and COOKIE per the request_order ini, so a same-named GET parameter overrides a value the code believed it read from $_POST. Repeated parameters using the a[]= syntax arrive as arrays, producing type confusion where string functions are expected (strlen(array) returns NULL on PHP 7 with a warning), and $_FILES['x']['name'] is client-controlled text that stays dangerous when trusted for storage names.

source_sink_clues.source: Query strings, form bodies and cookies — any superglobal whose keys the attacker controls — plus multipart field names and client file names.
source_sink_clues.sink: extract() on superglobals; parse_str() without a destination array; security checks reading variables name-matched to request keys via $_REQUEST; code trusting $_FILES name/type fields

tracking_guards: Require explicit key access ($_POST['k']) rather than symbol import; require the two-argument parse_str($s, $out) form; where extraction is unavoidable require EXTR_SKIP with a reserved prefix into a scope with no security-relevant variable names; require stored filenames to be regenerated server-side.
not_candidate_when: parse_str always writes into an explicit result array, extract imports into an isolated scope with EXTR_SKIP where no check variable names can collide, and upload names/paths are derived from server-side values rather than $_FILES metadata.
public_references: CWE-915: Improperly Controlled Modification of Dynamically-Determined Object Attributes — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/915.html
